versions.short: The bill would require hospitals, outpatient imaging centers, clinical laboratories, and ambulatory surgical centers to publish their standard prices online, free and in a machine-readable format, including the discounted cash price and the negotiated rates with insurers, and to update them quarterly. It would also require health plans and insurers to give patients price and cost-sharing information before care and to publish negotiated rate and payment data, and it would limit how group health plans' contracts with administrators can restrict their access to claims data. Providers that fail to comply could face civil penalties, and patients could be protected from paying amounts far above a good faith estimate or advance explanation of benefits. The bill would also require itemized bills on request and clearer explanations of benefits, and it would authorize appropriations for the Department of Labor and the Department of Health and Human Services to carry it out.
